rejected_experiments: Declaration-order permutations for list/sel/win_a/win_b/state/work/prev_sel/result (all pairwise orderings tried, including moving 'sel = 0' before vs after the three Func_08015010 calls, and moving 'list' to be the first-declared local of the function): stack-slot offsets for the six spilled locals (state/work/result/prev_sel/win_a/win_b) DO track declaration order directly -- getting win_a/win_b declared before state/work/result/prev_sel fixed all six stack offsets to match the reference exactly (this is retained) -- but no ordering of the two register-resident locals (list, sel) ever changed which of r6/r7 each received; the pair stayed r7=list/r6=sel throughout.

Splitting the do-while loop's 's32 i' into its own nested block vs a function-top-level declaration, and switching the outer loop between 'for(;;){...;if(result!=0)break;}' and 'do{...}while(result==0)': byte-identical output either way (both compile to the same test-at-bottom shape); kept the do-while form as marginally clearer.

Removing the '(void*)' cast on list at the two Func_080ab1f4 call sites, and declaring list as 'u8 *' instead of 's32' throughout (with a matching cast on its Func_08015010 assignment): no effect on the r6/r7 choice in either direction; reverted to 's32 list' to match select_quantity.c's own Func_08015010 s32-return precedent.

Reordering the commutative 'i + 0xC32' to '0xC32 + i' in the init loop's Func_08015080 call, and writing the second window-instruction message id as the literal '0xC31' vs the explicit 'the first constant plus one' ('0xC30 + 1'): both are folded identically by the compiler at parse time; no codegen change either way.

Introducing an explicit named local for the state->0x10C field ADDRESS (not value) instead of three separate M2C_FIELD(state,s32,0x10C) macro expansions: byte-identical output; the compiler already CSEs the repeated macro expansion into one address computation reused across the three call sites regardless, it just keeps choosing r5 for that computation where the reference chooses r6.

Rewriting every Data_03001e8c reference (not just the derived one at function entry) through the same '*(u8**)((u8*)&Data_03001f2c-0xA0)' address-of-arithmetic form used to fix the entry-point subs derivation (see the accepted fix below), including via a shared 'u8 **cell = (u8**)&Data_03001f2c' local reused for both state and work: no change to the late-function Data_03001e8c address-cache register (still r8 in the candidate vs r5 in the reference) in any form tried.

Accepted fix (kept, not rejected): expressing the function-entry reads as 'state = *(u8**)&Data_03001f2c;' followed by 'work = *(u8**)((u8*)&Data_03001f2c - 0xA0);' -- i.e. deriving Data_03001e8c's address arithmetically from Data_03001f2c's already-taken address, rather than reading the two globals independently -- reproduced the reference's 'subs r3,#160' exactly (previously a redundant second literal-pool load), dropping candidate_bytes 732->724 and wrong_instructions 206->190. This is the compiler recognizing the two fixed-address symbols as compile-time-foldable constants once their addresses are taken explicitly through '&', which a plain independent 'Data_03001e8c' global read does not trigger.

Accepted fix (kept, not rejected): splitting every 'sel = Func_080aa538(sel +/- 1, 7)' call into its own in-place 'sel += 1;'/'sel -= 1;' statement followed by 'sel = Func_080aa538(sel, 7);' -- matching the exact idiom documented in games/gs1/src/shop/select_use_item.c's own header comment for this same compiler -- reproduced the reference's in-place adds/subs-before-call instruction shape at all three call sites (previously the candidate folded the +/-1 into the call argument directly, a non-matching instruction order); this is a genuine structural correctness fix, independent of the register-swap residual, that further reduced wrong_instructions.

Semantic summary: a 7-item spinner-list selector reusing the same Data_03001f2c 'active menu' and Data_03001e8c 'UI text work' polymorphic cells as games/gs1/src/menu/select_quantity.c, but driving the shared low-level Func_08015xxx window/list kernel directly rather than through select_use_item.c's shop-specific wrappers. It draws two static instruction lines and a bordered box via the two already-adopted local helpers (Func_080ab1f4/Func_080ab2ec), builds a 7-entry text list (message ids 0xC32-0xC38), then loops: redraw the highlighted entry, poll input every frame for up/R (bits 0x90) or down/L (bits 0x60) to cycle the 7-item selection via Func_080aa538(value,7), B (Data_03001c94 bits 6 or 8) to cancel with result -1/-2, or A (bit 1) to confirm through a Func_08015048() validity gate before exiting with result 0/-1 style codes, clearing a per-slot list entry each pass, and finally re-registering the Func_080a19a0 periodic object-motion callback (also confirmed shared with select_quantity.c) before returning.

The two local callees this owner calls (Func_080ab1f4, Func_080ab2ec) are themselves not yet exact -- see games/gs1/recon/en/main/080ab21c.json for the third, Func_080ab21c, which both of those wrap and which remains a measured draft with its own documented residual (a GCD-factored offset expression). This owner's own score is independent of and does not depend on those being exact first, since all three are already the approved compiler's real emitted shape for this owner's call sites regardless of their own adoption status.

Field offsets 0x10 and 0x10C on the Data_03001f2c cell coincide exactly with struct CharacterSelectorState.selector_window (0x10C, games/gs1/src/menu/open_character_selector.c) and the analogous plain-s32 field read at select_quantity.c's own offset 16, and struct PsynergyMenuState also names both 0x10 (auxiliary_window) and 0x10C (message_window, games/gs1/include/psynergy_menu.h) -- suggestive but not owner-proven kinship, kept as an evidence note rather than an import, per Cleanroom's 'names no more specific than the evidence' rule.
